{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/sh

# Flux batch script (translated from Slurm)

# Slurm requested:
#   -A lu2020-2-7
#   -p lu
#   -t 2:00:00
#   -N 1
#   --tasks-per-node=1
#   --exclusive
#   -J snre_b
#   -o lunarc_output/lunarc_output_snre_hp_%j.out
#   -e lunarc_output/lunarc_output_snre_hp_%j.err
#   --mail-user=samuel.wiqvist@matstat.lu.se
#   --mail-type=ALL

flux alloc \
  -N 1 \
  -n 1 \
  --time=2h \
  --queue=lu \
  bash -lc '

mkdir -p lunarc_output

# Approximate Slurm %j output/error naming using Flux job id.
exec >"lunarc_output/lunarc_output_snre_hp_${FLUX_JOB_ID}.out" \
     2>"lunarc_output/lunarc_output_snre_hp_${FLUX_JOB_ID}.err"

# NOTE: Slurm -A lu2020-2-7 (account/project) has no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none for runtime, but accounting/charging/allocation association may be incorrect.

# NOTE: Slurm --exclusive has no universally portable Flux directive in a batch script.
# Performance implication: without exclusive-node allocation, you may share the node with other jobs, potentially
# causing performance variability due to resource contention.

# NOTE: Slurm email notifications (--mail-user/--mail-type) have no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none for runtime, but you will not receive job emails.

# NOTE: Slurm job name (-J snre_b) is not expressed here as a portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none (metadata only), but job identification in monitoring/accounting may be less clear.

ml load GCC/8.3.0
ml load CUDA/10.1.243
ml load OpenMPI/3.1.4
ml load PyTorch/1.6.0-Python-3.7.4

python /home/samwiq/snpla/seq-posterior-approx-w-nf-dev/two_moons/run_script_snre_b.py 1 2 11 10 8
'
"
}
